[[File:Incidence poset.svg|thumb|upright=1.35|A graph and its incidence poset]]

In [[mathematics]], an '''incidence poset''' or '''incidence order''' is a type of [[partially ordered set]] that represents the [[Incidence matrix|incidence relation]] between vertices and edges of an [[undirected graph]]. The incidence poset of a graph ''G'' has an element for each vertex or edge in ''G''. In this poset, there is an order relation ''x''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''y'' if and only if either ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''y'' or ''x'' is a vertex, ''y'' is an edge, and ''x'' is an endpoint of ([[incidence (graph theory)|incident]] to) ''y''.

==Example==
As an example, a [[zigzag poset]] or ''fence'' with an odd number of elements, with alternating order relations ''a''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''b''&nbsp;>&nbsp;''c''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''d''... is an incidence poset of a [[path graph]].

==Properties==
Every incidence poset of a non-empty graph has [[Antichain#Height and width|height]]&nbsp;two. Its width equals the number of edges plus the number of acyclic connected components.

Incidence posets have been particularly studied with respect to their [[order dimension]], and its relation to the properties of the underlying graph. The incidence poset of a connected graph ''G'' has order dimension at most two if and only if ''G'' is a path graph, and has order dimension at most three if and only if ''G'' is at most planar ([[Schnyder's theorem]]).<ref>{{citation
 | last = Schnyder | first = W.
 | doi = 10.1007/BF00353652
 | issue = 4
 | journal = [[Order (journal)|Order]]
 | pages = 323–343
 | title = Planar graphs and poset dimension
 | volume = 5
 | year = 1989| s2cid = 122785359
 }}.</ref> However, graphs whose incidence posets have order dimension&nbsp;4 may be [[dense graph|dense]]<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Agnarsson | first1 = Geir
 | last2 = Felsner | first2 = Stefan
 | last3 = Trotter | first3 = William T.
 | doi = 10.1016/S0012-365X(98)00309-4
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]
 | mr = 1687854
 | pages = 5–19
 | title = The maximum number of edges in a graph of bounded dimension, with applications to ring theory
 | volume = 201
 | year = 1999| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> and may have unbounded [[chromatic number]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Trotter | first1 = William T.
 | last2 = Wang | first2 = Ruidong
 | doi = 10.1007/s11083-013-9301-9
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Order (journal)|Order]]
 | pages = 279–287
 | title = Incidence posets and cover graphs
 | volume = 31
 | year = 2014| arxiv = 1308.2471| s2cid = 17560524
 }}.</ref> Every complete graph on ''n'' vertices, and by extension every graph on ''n'' vertices, has an incidence poset with order dimension ''O''(log&nbsp;log&nbsp;''n'').<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Hoşten | first1 = Serkan
 | last2 = Morris | first2 = Walter D. Jr.
 | doi = 10.1016/S0012-365X(98)00315-X
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]
 | mr = 1687882
 | pages = 133–139
 | title = The order dimension of the complete graph
 | volume = 201
 | year = 1999| doi-access = 
 }}.</ref> If an incidence poset has high dimension then it must contain copies of the incidence posets of all small trees either as sub-orders or as the duals of sub-orders.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Brightwell | first1 = Graham R.
 | last2 = Trotter | first2 = William T.
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01108600
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Order (journal)|Order]]
 | mr = 1302404
 | pages = 159–167
 | title = Incidence posets of trees in posets of large dimension
 | volume = 11
 | year = 1994| s2cid = 120777046
 }}.</ref>

== Incidence poset of vertices, edges and faces ==
[[File:Incidence poset of vertices, edges and faces.png|thumb|upright=1.35|a planar map with its incidence poset of vertices, edges and faces]]
Given a planar map, a [[planar graph]] with a fixed plane embedding, one can look at the incidence poset of vertices, edges and faces. The resulting incidence poset then has height three and is given by the natural incidence relations between vertices, edges, and faces. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Felsner |first=Stefan |title=The Order Dimension of Planar Maps Revisited |url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/130945284 |journal=SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics |language=en |volume=28 |issue=3 |pages=1093–1101 |doi=10.1137/130945284 |issn=0895-4801|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

For a planar map, the order dimension of their incidence poset is at most four.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brightwell |first=Graham R. |last2=Trotter |first2=William T. |title=The Order Dimension of Planar Maps |url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/S0895480192238561 |journal=SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics |language=en |volume=10 |issue=4 |pages=515–528 |doi=10.1137/S0895480192238561 |issn=0895-4801|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
